intro: Selling insurance builds persuasion, negotiation and steady client service, all prized in finance. Among the 25 careers below, the closest fits are Loan Officers and Personal Financial Advisors, both at an 88% skill match. Advisors earn a BLS May 2025 median of $105,070, or 69% more than the $62,280 agents earn.
why_it_works: You explain complex products, handle objections and keep a book of clients for years. O*NET rates persuasion at 3.62 out of 5 for this job, and time management at 3.5, the same strengths that lending, underwriting and financial advising use. Every match needs no more education than you already have. The gap is depth with numbers: budgets, risk analysis and complex problem solving.
tips: Your license and client list are assets; note your retention rate and premium volume on your resume.
Underwriting is a quieter move: Insurance Underwriters earn $81,370, which is 31% more, and use the same product knowledge.
Study for financial planning credentials while still selling, so you can move to advising without a pay gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former insurance sales agents do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Loan Officers (88%), Personal Financial Advisors (88%) and Insurance Underwriters (86%), based on O*NET 31.0. Loan Officers earn a median of $76,690, which is 23% more than the $62,280 insurance agent median, and they also work on commission with clients you may already know.

faq.q: Which careers for insurance agents pay more?
faq.a: 20 of the 25 matches pay more than insurance sales. Marketing Managers earn $166,790 (168% more), Financial Managers $166,570 (167% more) and Sales Managers $148,270 (138% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. These manager roles usually need years of experience first.

faq.q: Do insurance sales agents need another degree?
faq.a: No for all 25 matches: each usually needs no more education than an agent already has. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 69% of workers in the closest match, so licenses, sales results and a long client track record count most when you apply.

faq.q: What skills should insurance agents build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing financial resources, managing materials, judgment and decision making and complex problem solving. Service orientation already rates 3.38 out of 5 for agents in O*NET, so analysis rather than people skills is the gap.
